drug_class: Anticholinergic eye drop (mydriatic and cycloplegic agent)
purpose: Tropicamide is an eye drop used by eye doctors to dilate your pupils during an eye exam. It temporarily widens your pupils so the doctor can get a better look at the back of your eye, including the retina and optic nerve. It can also temporarily relax the focusing muscles in your eye during certain eye tests.
how_it_works: Your pupils are controlled by tiny muscles that respond to signals from your nervous system. Tropicamide blocks a specific chemical signal called acetylcholine, which normally keeps your pupil from getting too big. By blocking that signal, the muscles relax, your pupil opens wide, and light can reach deeper into your eye so the doctor can see clearly inside.
common_side_effects: Blurry vision and sensitivity to bright light are very common and expected — this is the whole point of the drops! You may also notice a mild stinging or burning right when the drops go in. Some people feel a slight headache or have trouble focusing up close for a few hours.
warnings: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until your vision fully returns to normal, which usually takes 4 to 8 hours. Wear sunglasses after your appointment because your eyes will be very sensitive to light. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma or a family history of it, as these drops can rarely trigger a dangerous pressure spike in the eye. Keep out of reach of children, as accidental swallowing can be very dangerous for kids.
typical_dosing: An eye doctor or their technician will place 1 to 2 drops in each eye about 15 to 30 minutes before your exam. The effects usually last between 4 and 8 hours. This medication is used in the office setting and is not typically something you take at home on your own.
